author: Bryan White

pilot.role: Chief Investment Officer of a corporate pension plan
pilot.task: a corporate defined-benefit pension's return-seeking and credit portfolio: about $3B of liabilities, 92% funded, liability hedging run separately, a 6% nominal return target net of fees, a drawdown limit of about 25% in a severe episode, investment-grade credit welcome as a partial liability match, no cash floor and no private markets.
pilot.baseline_basis: pilot's estimate, including getting the team together, booking meetings and back-and-forth, “if I'm on top of the team, nagging as I do”
pilot.quote: It's definitely cool to see the different agents debate and work the problem.
pilot.what_they_would_change: The user experience: make the reasoning followable. “Maybe you need a secretary agent to better document the whole thing.”
feedback: I wasn't able to follow its logic, which would have been helpful, in terms of its starting points, what its constraints were, data sources, etc.
Following the committee meeting was cool. I like the idea of a red team but couldn't follow what they were objecting to.
The quant was the most important committee member, but again couldn't follow logic.
Probably 30 minutes reviewing, but that's because it wasn't intuitive. As I kept reviewing I was better able to put the pieces together.
pilot.notes: The 7 minutes include one failed first attempt on the hosted app; the cause was not captured (a redeploy of the hosted app during the session is the likely cause). The second attempt completed.
pilot.lesson: The pilot valued the committee and the Red Team but could not follow the reasoning: the app records everything (evidence ids, a full audit trace, per-agent summaries) but does not explain it to a reader. Transparency for an auditor is not the same as explanation for a decision-maker. A secretary agent that writes the committee minutes (starting assumptions, constraints, data sources, each objection in plain language and what changed because of it) is the first item I would build next.
